required_knowns.claim: Relations are explicitly supplied. The snapshot records endpoints, deterministic relation identities, whole endpoint-file hashes and the local repository revision. It does not infer relations or store complete source contents.

A successful check compares whole named endpoint files. Changed content or a recordable endpoint failure (missing, unsafe_path, not_regular or unsupported_text) makes the result and incident edges needs_review; unaffected edges can remain current. Edits outside a cited line still count. Other failures, including byte limits, remain errors rather than freshness results.

Endpoint freshness, HEAD change and dirty-state reporting are separate. Unchanged named files can yield current with revision_changed=true after an unrelated commit. An unlisted ADR is not added to the graph or semantically assessed; an untracked file can still affect the conservative dirty signal.

Relations remain unverified, including verified_by and supersedes. Current does not establish passing tests, implementation compliance, accepted decision status or corpus completeness. Supersession requires reading source and status; provenance does not establish semantic truth.

Snapshot publishes a new local research JSON artifact without overwriting an existing output; check returns evidence without updating that snapshot. The shipped contract does not import document nodes into codegraph or edit project history. History retrieval and source reading remain separate steps.

expected_unknowns: The semantic truth of a declared relation, the accepted status of a superseding ADR and actual test results require additional evidence.
The manifest does not establish whether unlisted contradictory or superseding evidence exists.
Behavior of external consumers and end-to-end Lens/history integration is outside this source allowlist. No execution was performed.
materially_false_claims: Check inserts newly discovered ADR nodes or imports document relationships into the native codegraph.
Current or verified_by proves acceptance, compliance or passing tests.
Every HEAD change invalidates every graph edge.
Unchanged HEAD guarantees endpoint freshness or complete evidence.
All endpoint read failures produce needs_review rather than an error.
Check rewrites the snapshot or project history, or snapshot overwrites existing output.
reviewer_notes: A separate read-only agent reviewed the claims and anchors against the exact source revision. The coordinator applied the distinction between an untracked-file dirty signal and semantic graph discovery. This is agent source review, not runtime evidence, human sign-off or model-quality measurement.
A successful snapshot is an explicit premise: a schema-valid manifest alone does not establish readable files or in-range endpoint lines.
The conservative dirty signal may change on a metadata-only touch. Do not require a content change or complete unlisted-file discovery from that flag.
